author: feral-core
description: Software-engineering and general local-computer surface: repository-scoped file edits (read/write/edit with anchor-based replacements), codebase search (grep/glob), shell commands (git, package managers, test/build runners, ad-hoc one-liners), and HTTP fetch for docs/APIs. Shell commands run on the host inside a folder the operator granted; outside every grant they are refused and the operator is asked for access. This is FERAL's single canonical shell + filesystem toolset.

endpoints.description: Execute a shell command and return stdout/stderr. Use for running programs, git, npm, pip, pytest, etc. Runs on the host in `cwd`, which must resolve inside a folder the operator granted; a command whose cwd or path arguments fall outside every grant is refused with `permission_needed` so the operator can grant access.

params.name: command
params.description: The shell command to execute

params.name: cwd
params.description: Working directory to run in. Defaults to FERAL_CWD, then FERAL_WORKSPACE, then the brain's own directory. Must resolve inside a granted folder.

params.name: timeout
params.description: Timeout in seconds (default 30)

endpoints.returns_description: stdout, stderr, exit code, and the execution mode used (host_workspace or docker)

endpoints.description: Read the contents of a file. Returns the text content with line numbers.

params.name: path
params.description: Absolute or relative file path

params.name: offset
params.description: Start reading from this line (1-based)

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of lines to read

endpoints.description: Create or overwrite a file with the given content.

params.name: path
params.description: File path to write to

params.name: content
params.description: The content to write

endpoints.returns_description: Confirmation of file creation with byte count

endpoints.description: Search and replace text in a file. Prefer text copied verbatim from coding_tools__read_file. If the exact text is not found, a chain of fallback matchers (line-trimmed, whitespace-normalised, indentation-flexible, escape-normalised, and last a first/last-line block anchor) tries to locate the same block; the strategy that succeeded is reported back as match_strategy. Text matching more than one place is always refused, never guessed at: add surrounding context, or set replace_all when every occurrence should change.

params.name: path
params.description: File path to edit

params.name: old_text
params.description: Text to find. Must identify exactly one location unless replace_all is set.

params.name: new_text
params.description: Replacement text

params.name: replace_all
params.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring old_text to be unique (default false).

params.name: expected_replacements
params.description: Fail unless exactly this many occurrences are found. Use it as a checksum when you already know the count.

endpoints.returns_description: {path, replacements, match_strategy, matched_lines} on success, plus diagnostics when a checker exists for the file type. On failure: error_code (not_found / ambiguous / unexpected_replacement_count / oversized_span) and, when nothing matched, closest_match with the real file text nearest to old_text.

endpoints.description: Search for a regex pattern in files (ripgrep-backed). Defaults to returning matching FILE NAMES (output_mode='files_with_matches'), which is cheap and best for narrowing; ask for output_mode='content' only after you know which files matter. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

params.name: pattern
params.description: Regex pattern to search for

params.name: path
params.description: Directory or file to search in (default: current directory)

params.name: include
params.description: File glob pattern to include (e.g. '*.py')

params.name: output_mode
params.description: 'files_with_matches' (default: file names), 'content' (lines with line numbers), or 'count' (per-file counts). Prefer files_with_matches first to save context.

params.name: head_limit
params.description: Max results (default 250; 0 = unlimited). Truncated responses include pagination.next_offset.

params.name: offset
params.description: Skip first N results before head_limit (paging large result sets).

endpoints.returns_description: files_with_matches: {mode, files[], total_files}; content: {mode, matches[{file,line,text}], total}; count: {mode, counts[]}. Truncated results include {truncated, pagination}.

endpoints.description: Find files matching a glob pattern (ripgrep-backed, respects .gitignore, most-recently-modified first). Useful for discovering project structure. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

params.name: pattern
params.description: Glob pattern (e.g. '**/*.py', 'src/**/*.ts')

params.name: path
params.description: Root directory to search from (default: current directory)

params.name: head_limit
params.description: Max files to return (default 100; 0 = unlimited). Truncated responses set {truncated: true}.

endpoints.returns_description: {files[], total, truncated?}: files relative to workspace root, newest first

endpoints.description: Fetch a URL and return its content as readable text (HTML stripped).

params.name: url
params.description: The URL to fetch

params.name: max_length
params.description: Max characters to return (default 10000)

endpoints.description: Undo the file writes made while answering one user message. Restores each file to the content it had before the turn started, from FERAL's own content-addressed checkpoints (no git involved, so the user's index and stash are untouched). Files that changed after FERAL wrote them are listed and skipped unless force is set. Shell commands are NOT checkpointed, so anything coding_tools__bash changed is not reverted.

params.name: turn_id
params.description: Turn to revert. Defaults to the most recent checkpointed turn in this session.

params.name: force
params.description: Revert files that changed after FERAL wrote them, discarding those changes. Off by default.

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Report what would be reverted without touching any file.

endpoints.returns_description: {turn_id, reverted[], reverted_count, skipped[], drifted[], files[], bash_not_covered, note}
